title: New charge against Toronto cop accused in teen's suicide
subtitle: SIU adds breach of trust to charges against officer that already include criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessaries of life.
article: A Toronto cop accused of negligence causing death in a man's suicide at High Park last winter was hit with a new charge on Thursday.
Const. Kyle Upjohn, 33, was charged with breach of trust in connection to a man's death at the west end park on Feb. 2.
He was also charged by Ontario's police watchdog in June with criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessaries of life.
Upjohn did not attend court in downtown Toronto on Thursday to hear the new charge. He was represented by Daniel Lee, who stood in for Upjohn's lawyer as a designate.
Lee declined to comment about the case as he left the courthouse.
In a statement Thursday, the Special Investigations Unit announced the third charge but did not explain why it was laid later than the first two.
The SIU did not immediately respond to questions from the Star.

At the time of the original charges in June, the SIU said Toronto police were contacted around 2 p.m. on Feb. 2, regarding a suicide attempt by a 19-year-old man at High Park. By 3:30 p.m., the SIU wrote, the 19-year-old was pronounced dead.
Alexandre Boucher is identified as the deceased in court documents detailing Upjohn's charges. Boucher's family has declined to speak publicly about his death.
The SIU investigates instances across Ontario where a civilian is seriously injured, killed, or sexually assaulted during an interaction with police.
